name: 207. MCP OAuth server on localhost follows the private allowlist (mcp-oauth-private-allowlist)
description:
Management-endpoint checks with no live provider involved. The MCP OAuth chain (discovery, dynamic client registration, token requests) dials through a public-only guard, so an OAuth-protected MCP server on localhost could not be added by anyone, not even an authenticated admin. Hosts on mcp_oauth_private_allowlist (config.json mcp.tool_manager_config.oauth_private_allowlist) are now reachable for MCP clients registered by an authenticated caller; link-local and metadata addresses stay blocked and clients registered with auth bypassed stay public-only. The harness profile allowlists localhost, 127.0.0.1 and ::1, and every row carries the setup token, so these rows run as an authenticated caller.

Prerequisite: examples/mcps/oauth-demo-server listening on localhost:3003 (cd examples/mcps/oauth-demo-server && go run .). Nothing in the harness runners starts it, so the second row is [PREVIEW]-tagged: run FEATURE="mcp-oauth-private-allowlist" INCLUDE_PREVIEW=1 once the server is up. The first row reads the allowlist back from the store; the second registers an OAuth MCP client against the demo server and expects the pending_oauth response carrying the demo server's authorize URL. The consent is never completed, so no MCP client row is created; the pending OAuth config it leaves behind is inert.
